div.head: VIII Atr 28
div.ab: Gif weofodþen be boca tæcincge his agen lif rihtlice fadige, þonne sy he fulles þegnweres ⁊ weorðscipes wurðe ge on life ge on legere.
Gif weofodþen be boca tæcincge his agen lif rihtlice fadige, þonne sy he fulles þegnweres ⁊ weorðscipes wurðe, ge on life ge on legere.
Gif weofodþen be boca tæcincge his agen lif rihtlice fadige, þonne sy he fulles þegnweres and weorðscipes wurðe, ge on life ge on legere.
Wenn ein Altardiener nach Vorschrift der Kanones sein eigenes Leben gesetzmässig regelt, dann sei er vollen Thegn-Wergeldes und Ehrenranges theilhaftig, so im Leben wie im Grabe.
If a servant of the altar orders his own life lawfully according to the teaching of the books [canons], then let him be entitled to a full thegn's wergild and honour, both in life and in the grave.

If a member of the priesthood orders his own life aright, according to the teaching of the canon law, he shall be entitled to the full wergeld and privileges of a thegn, both during his life and after his death.

If a minister of the altar order his own life rightly according to the instruction of the books [of canon law], he is then to be entitled to the full wergild and dignity of a thegn, both in life and in the grave.
If a priest who serves at the altar conducts his life properly according to canon law, then he is to be deemed worthy of the full wergild and privileges of a thane, both in life and after death.
div.note: Some of Liebermann’s notes here are cut off in the gutter of the scan used, and are still to be completed.
Chapters 28–30 form an 11th-c. ‘Additamentum’ to the Canons of Edgar 60 (ed. Thorpe, Ancient Laws 401). Liebermann compares VI Atr 5.3.
